notes.title: Major Performance Optimizations and Improved Controller Experience
notes.content:
[list]
[*] We've optimized game performance: Astro Looter can now achieve peak frame rates of [b]300 FPS[/b] on [u]RTX 2060-era[/u] hardware with max settings, with an average frame rate exceeding [b]120 FPS[/b]. On [u]GTX 1050 or equivalent[/u] hardware, the game maintains a stable [b]60 FPS[/b] during normal gameplay.
[*] Reduced VRAM usage, lowering the likelihood of crashes on some hardware during startup.
[*] [u][b]Fully rebuilt the UI system[/b][/u], significantly enhancing the controller-based UI experience.
[/list]

notes.title: New Weapon Overclock Skills and UI Optimization
notes.content:
1. [b]Weapon Overclock:[/b] When a weapon reaches levels 2, 6, and 10, and after upgrading 9 times using weapon upgrade [orange card] (excluding Projectile cards) in game, the ultimate overclock ability will be triggered. Examples include:

[b]High-Explosive Rounds:[/b] Bullets generate shockwave damage upon explosion.
[b]Hydrogen Fuel:[/b] Produces blue flames with higher damage.
[b]Mini Prism: [/b] Adds mini prisms that cause some rays to scatter.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44991943/176d8fd7caa71af8da1afcd60a6afc2e08de1747.gif[/img]

Additionally, after overclocking, the selected weapon upgrade cards will be enhanced.

[u]We've uploaded videos showcasing all weapon effects on the Vault page for players to view.[/u]

2. [b]UI Improvements: [/b]
    - Weapon upgrade previews now display post-upgrade values (currently support mouse only).
    - Added an indicator for the number of crystals required to unlock on the map selection page.

3. [b]Gameplay Adjustments: [/b]Optimized the difficulty of levels on the first planet.

4. [b]Bug fix:[/b] Attempted to resolve the issue where some users were unable to enter the game and received the "Please Launch From Steam" message.

5. Minor bug fixes and performance optimizations.

notes.content:
[b]1. Fixed the issue where players temporarily stop moving after constructing buildings.

notes.title: Crash Issue Fix Report - 18 July
notes.content:
Due to the recent increase in crash incidents, which have significantly impacted your gaming experience, we have swiftly investigated the issues and released multiple updates over the past few days. [u]The issue is nearly resolved, but we are continuing to monitor it.[/u] We understand that we cannot undo the issues that have already occurred, but we hope this report can share some information and demonstrate our commitment to the player experience.

[h2]Crash Stat:[/h2]
Versions before July 12: Average crash rate - 0%
Versions from July 12 to July 14: Average crash rate - 18.4%
Versions from July 14 to July 16: Average crash rate - 32.1%
Version from July 17: Average crash rate - 14.1%
Version from July 18: Average crash rate - 0.025%
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44991943/72dbbf1bf5bb7dff7a575b7b7681dc726651e821.png[/img]


Based on anonymous cloud log reports, the recent crashes are caused by the following two issues:
[h2]Issue 1:[/h2]
[h3]In simple terms:[/h3]
This issue is caused by changes in the total number of buildings in the scene, particularly when reduced, leading to an out-of-bounds array query in the C++ code for querying buildings, resulting in a crash.

[h3]The Boring Part:[/h3]
When enemies patrol, they check for nearby heroes or buildings. If there are both buildings and heroes nearby, they prioritize attacking heroes; otherwise, they attack buildings. When the AI patrol system retrieves the building list, a change in the list during this process causes a null pointer issue in C++, leading to an out-of-bounds array query and a crash.

The occurrence probability of this issue is positively correlated with device performance. Due to the high performance of our development machines, we did not replicate the issue in our lab environment, delaying the fix.

[h3]Solution:[/h3]
We have modified the code execution order and added boundary and pointer checks. Based on cloud logs, the patch released on July 18 has significantly reduced the occurrence of this issue, with no further occurrences reported. We are continuously monitoring the issue and will release further fix reports as needed.

[h2]Issue 2:[/h2]
[h3]In simple terms:[/h3]
This issue occurs when the turret's material is changed during tower construction, leading to a crash due to an incorrect material replacement.

[h3]The Boring Part:[/h3]
During tower construction, the turret's material is changed and a material animation is played. During this process, a low-level error might cause an attempt to access a non-existent material, resulting in the failure of setting the instance material or shader material parameters, leading to an OS crash.

[h3]Solution:[/h3]
This issue has a relatively low occurrence probability. We have added boundary and pointer checks. Based on cloud logs, this issue has not reoccurred, but we will continue to monitor it.

Our team has been working at full speed over the past few days to resolve these severe crashes. We apologize for the negative experience caused. If you no longer encounter crash issues after updating to the latest version, please feel free to let others know. If the problem persists, please continue to inform us. Thank you for your support and attention.

notes.title: Important Update Fixes Crash Issue When Building Defense Towers
notes.content:
After thorough tracking, we identified a critical issue that caused the game to crash when players built defense towers. This was due to a series of erroneous C++ codes leading to a difficult-to-detect array out-of-bounds problem. By analyzing the cloud crash log data, we believe we have resolved the crash issues for most players. Please update to the latest version to ensure the best user experience. This fix also includes optimizations for some performance overheads.

While we have made significant efforts to greatly reduce the likelihood of crashes, we cannot entirely eliminate all crash issues due to variations in hardware performance. If you continue to encounter problems, please contact us. We deeply apologize for the poor experience during the initial release and hope for your understanding.

notes.title: Major Update: Enhanced Gameplay Experience with New Enemies and Improved Combat
notes.content:
- New Enemy: Acid Spitter Spider - An annoying ranged attacker that spits splashing acid, damaging heroes.
- New Enemy: Magma Smasher - A big guy with magma inside; upon death, it leaves behind magma that can harm heroes.
- New Enemy: Giant Chameleon Moth - A hard-to-spot roaming creature made of Titan minerals. It doesn’t actively attack heroes.
- The map screen now displays the highest star rating and difficulty level for completed rounds.
- Thrust cooldown is now linked to hero level—the higher the hero level, the shorter the cooldown.
- Combat Feedback: Added bone-crushing effects when enemies die.
- Combat Feedback: Improved blood effects when enemy take damage.
- Adjusted and optimized background music for the end of stages.
- Added multi-channel audio settings in the options menu.
- Fixed an issue where the number scroll on the stage results screen took too long.
